item.title: Oyebanji seeks FG support for livestock development
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has sought increased Federal Government support and collaboration to expand livestock development, create jobs and boost economic opportunities in the state. Oyebanji made the appeal on Tuesday while receiving the Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who was in the state to commission an ultra-modern veterinary hospital in Ado-Ekiti and inspect ongoing projects under the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (LPRESS) programme. The governor said livestock development had enormous potential to improve agricultural productivity, generate wealth, create employment and strengthen livelihoods. He called for stronger collaboration between the state and the Federal Government to harness opportunities in the sector, particularly through interventions aimed at improving livestock production and developing its value chain. Oyebanji commended President Bola Tinubu for establishing a separate Ministry of Livestock Development, describing agriculture and livestock as critical sectors for job creation and economic growth. He said his administration was committed to working with the Federal Government, investors and other stakeholders to unlock the sector’s potential and position Ekiti as an attractive destination for livestock investment. The governor urged the minister to assess the state’s ongoing projects, particularly the Ikun Dairy Farm, where he said federal intervention was needed to expand operations and improve sustainability. “I don’t believe in noise making; I believe the only way to advertise yourself is by showcasing your achievements,” he said. He added that the state had reached a stage where additional Federal Government support was necessary to enable its livestock initiatives to achieve greater impact. Earlier, Maiha commended Oyebanji for prioritising agriculture as a means of tackling poverty and unemployment, creating wealth and expanding economic opportunities. The minister assured the governor of the Federal Government’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with Ekiti to expand the agricultural value chain, increase production and sustain the state’s efforts towards food security. Maiha said his working visit included the commissioning of the veterinary hospital and inspection of LPRESS projects across the state. The facilities scheduled for inspection included the Ikun Dairy Farm, Emure Poultry Hub, cattle market in Ado-Ekiti, the ongoing construction of a semi-automated abattoir and the Erifun Broiler Processing Plant in Ado-Ekiti, among others. Also present at the meeting were the Chief of Staff, Niyi Adebayo; Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Security, Ebenezer Boluwade; Special Adviser on Media, Yinka Oyebode; and LPRESS State Coordinator, Olayinka Adedipe. The post Oyebanji seeks FG support for livestock development appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: WWE’s Liv Morgan, Judgment Day totally nail Shrek Halloween costumes
item.description: WWE’s Liv Morgan, Judgment Day totally nail Shrek Halloween costumes appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It’s always fun to see what WWE Superstars dress up as for Halloween , and Liv Morgan , Dominik Mysterio , and the Judgment Day nailed their Shrek-inspired costumes. The faction dressed up as various characters from the animated franchise. Naturally, on-screen couple Morgan and Mysterio were Shrek and Princess Fiona. View this post on Instagram Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Raquel Rodriguez dressed up as Donkey, while JD McDonagh dressed up as Lord Farquaad and Roxanne Perez dressed up as the Gingerbread Man. Fans had a lot to say in the comments section. One joked that Sami Zayn “might have PTSD if he sees Roxy,” which is a reference to the Undisputed WWE Champion’s feud with Trick Williams. McDonagh got a lot of attention for his outfit. One fan commented, “Not sure if JD [is] in a costume,” while another said, “Bruh I think big head is an upgrade. JD downgrading to Lord Farquaad is absolutely crazy work.” The size of his head is the butt of many jokes in WWE. Some fans appreciated him embracing them, with one saying, “At least JD is embracing his twin Lord Farquaad.” Shrek is an iconic animated movie franchise that started in 2001. Four films have been released, and a fifth—the first since Shrek Forever After in 2010—is coming in June 2027. Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, and Cameron Diaz lead the franchise, which has also spawned two spin-off movies. The Judgment Day is gearing up for Crown Jewel. The Women’s World Champion, Morgan, is set to face the Women’s Champion, Chelsea Green, in the Women’s Crown Jewel Championship match. More than likely, her Judgment Day stablemates will come out and try to help her win. Over the years, WWE’s Judgment Day stable has changed its lineup. Originally, it started with Edge and Damian Priest. Rhea Ripley and Finn Bálor were later added. Bálor’s introduction to the group resulted in Edge being ousted. They later added Mysterio, McDonagh, Carlito, Morgan, Rodriguez, and Perez. Now, the group’s lineup consists of Morgan, Mysterio, McDonagh, Rodriguez, and Perez. item.title: French blood banks hacked in latest cyber-attack on Europe
item.description: Temperature and defrosting thresholds raised to ‘very high levels’ at three cold stores stocking vital blood products France’s national blood service has said hackers accessed control systems and boosted temperatures at three cold stores stocking vital blood products, in an apparent escalation of recent cyber-attacks on fridges and freezers across Europe. The French blood service (EFS) said temperature and defrosting thresholds had been raised to “very high levels” in the attack, adding that its alarm systems had allowed technicians to intervene before the products were compromised. item.title: Dodgers notes: Tarik Skubal, Shohei Ohtani
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the first inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Free agency has officially begun, and the Dodgers are now on the clock to try to fortify their roster before the impending lockout. Left-hander Tarik Skubal is atop the list of the most highly coveted free agents this offseason, and the Dodgers are not the only bidder for his services. Jeff Passan at ESPN reports that the New York Mets will compete with the Dodgers for the highest offer, while the Chicago Cubs want Skubal “badly.” The two most obvious suitors are the two teams with the highest payrolls in baseball: The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets. There are bound to be others. The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get — well in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range. Alden Gonzalez of ESPN is more optimistic about the chances of Skubal returning to Los Angeles for 2027 and beyond. He truly seemed to relish his 2½ months in Los Angeles. He loved the culture, particularly being among so many established, veteran players who were singularly focused on winning. He became besties with Blake Snell, was awed by the organization’s resources and, overall, seemed to fit in seamlessly. Buster Olney of ESPN shared his thoughts on what type of deal Skubal is projected for, noting that a deal for him would resemble Kyle Tucker’s current deal with the Dodgers compared to Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s record setting deal. After two fantastic years of Shohei Ohtani in Dodger blue, the two-way superstar and still reigning two-time NL MVP award winner mired in a power drought in the second half and beyond that rendered him obsolete in the starting lineup. That was until he hit a towering three-run home run that gave the Dodgers their final runs of the 2026 postseason. David Adler of MLB.com notes that Ohtani’s Game 4 home run in the NLCS could help him get back on track hitting-wise before the start of the 2027 season. When we’re seeing Ohtani connect with the baseball with bat speeds like that, we know his swing is in the right place. Are we overanalyzing one home run? Maybe! But we think that one home run was a harbinger of what’s coming next year: the return of MVP-level Ohtani.

item.title: NFL Gross Quarterback Ranks: What do we think about Michael Penix Jr.?
item.description: How much stock can you put in a quarterback stuck in a constant downpour? That's the question NFL fans are asking after Michael Penix Jr. continued his roller coaster career with a gruesome performance in swampy Tampa Bay. Penix had more interceptions Sunday than the Buccaneers had pass attempts, clearing the way for him to surge to the top of this week's Gross Quarterback Rankings. But at least he can blame the weather. Jacoby Brissett, on the other hand, was playing the league's worst defense in a dome. There's no perfect metric for a quarterback's impact, but expected points added (EPA) helps measure their ability to swing the outcome of a game through the air, on the ground and through avoiding negative plays. Last year, EPA told us Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford were a cut above the rest of the league's quarterbacks in the regular season, netting 151.3 and 120.3 EPA , respectfully. No one else in the league topped triple digits. Unsurprisingly, those two led playoff teams and finished second and first, respectively, in MVP voting. We can use EPA to help dissect which quarterbacks underwhelmed the hardest in their debut. By comparing their Week 8 EPA across their early 2026 season averages, we get a better idea of whose fans should be most annoyed. And so, we end up with a "worst QBs" list that doesn't include Cam Ward or even Bo Nix, simply because their starts to the season have been so disappointing we've been moderately conditioned not to expect more this fall. You have to be at least decent in 2026 — or otherworldly awful on a given week — to wind up in the gross QB rankings. We'll also look at completion percentage over expected (CPOE), which gives you a good idea of which quarterbacks are making tough throws (and, in some cases, being bailed out by exceptional catches). All data come from NFL Pro. We'll also keep a running tally of the times each quarterback lands here. We'll score that placement track meet style — 10 points for first place, then eight, six, four, two and one — in order to figure out who was truly 2026's grossest passer. Honorable mention: Justin Herbert, Los Angeles Chargers 2026 EPA/game : -9.3 Week 8 EPA : -19.7 Difference : 10.4 points worse 2026 CPOE : -3.5 percent Week 8 CPOE : 2.2 percent Difference : 5.7 points better The Chargers continue to find ways to make things worse. Herbert emerged from the bye week and played roughly as badly as he had in Week 6. He's thrown zero touchdowns but three interceptions in his last two games. His average pass distance dipped to a season-low five yards downfield against the Los Angeles Rams , allowing offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel to further his groundbreaking research into destroying the Chargers. 5. item.title: The second act nobody saw coming: Steven Alker's remarkable rise at 50
item.description: Five years ago, on a warm practice day at the PGA Tour Champions' Furyk & Friends tournament in Jacksonville, Florida, an unassuming New Zealander named Steven Alker was quietly working on the driving range. Few spectators stopped to watch. Fewer still could have imagined what was about to unfold. But one man saw something special. John Felice, a volunteer from Ponte Vedra Beach working the range, stood alongside a reporter and pointed toward Alker. "You need to watch this guy," he said. "He's got the most beautiful swing." The prediction proved remarkably prophetic. Alker was a journeyman At the time, Alker hardly appeared destined for stardom. He was a journeyman professional who had spent decades grinding through the highs and lows of a game that rarely rewards persistence. He chased opportunities around the globe, trying to carve out a living while remaining largely anonymous to golf fans. Meanwhile, the reporter was occupied tracking down more recognizable names such as quote machines Rocco Mediate and Paul Goydos, players who would eventually finish somewhere around 40th that week. Alker barely registered on anyone's radar. That was about to change. Making his way originally as a Monday qualifier, he finished tied for seventh, extending a remarkable streak of six consecutive top-10 finishes that season. Less than a month later, he captured his first PGA Tour Champions title, launching one of the most remarkable late-career renaissances in professional golf. For Scott McCarron, Alker's rise remains difficult to comprehend. "We all just wonder, where was he 20 years ago, you know what I mean?" McCarron said. It's a fair question. Alker's PGA Tour career was unspectacular In 87 career starts on the PGA Tour, Alker never recorded a top-10 finish. He earned less than $1 million competing against the world's best players and appeared destined to remain one of professional golf's forgettable names. Yet golf has a way of offering second chances, and Alker has taken full advantage of golf’s ultimate mulligan at age 50. The New Zealander has become one of the most successful unsung players in PGA Tour Champions history. He won the 2023 Charles Schwab Cup , has amassed 14 victories on the senior circuit and continues to perform at a level few could have imagined during his PGA Tour years. Now 55, he's showing little sign of slowing down. Alker recorded four victories and 12 top-10 finishes this season while pushing his PGA Tour Champions career earnings beyond $15 million. He enters this week's Charles Schwab Cup Championship in Phoenix ranked third in the standings. The formula, according to his peers, isn't complicated. It's execution. "He possesses one of the soundest swings on Tour, and he's a great putter," McCarron said. "Once he learned how to win, there was no stopping the guy. He has no weaknesses." item.title: No Bones About It: Hyland’s Stats Show He’s Stepping Up With Edwards Out
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Bones Hyland (8) works around Milwaukee Bucks center Jericho Sims (00) in the first quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor It was obvious that the Timberwolves needed someone to step up in the wake of Anthony Edwards ‘ knee injury. But it wasn’t obvious that it would be Bones Hyland . Hyland was barely playing before Edwards’ injury , and he’s still not getting huge minutes. However, Hyland’s stats in the four games since Edwards went out show that he’s taking advantage of the minutes he does get and has raised his game perhaps as much as any of the Timberwolves. Edwards’ Injury Paved The Way For More Meaningful Minutes Hyland struggled to crack coach Chris Finch’s regular rotation at the start of the season, which was a bit surprising. He was a valuable contributor off the bench last year, particularly after the Timberwolves traded for Ayo Dosunmu and the two earned the nickname “ Twin Turbos ” with their fast-paced play. Hyland started this season as the fifth player off the bench and was largely relegated to mop-up duty in the four games before Edwards’ injury. The only exception was a 117-94 win against Toronto, where Hyland played 15 minutes. He was great defensively in that game, notching three blocks and two steals. But he shot 0-5. In the four games since Edwards’ injury, Hyland’s has been thrust into the regular rotation and is averaging 16 meaningful minutes per game. Increased production has followed. Hyland’s Stats Are Way Up Based On Volume Bones had a total of nine points and four assists in the four games before Edwards went out. He’s averaging 12.0 points and 4.25 assists per game in the four games since. The highlight was a 19-point, eight-assist performance in a win over the Los Angeles Clippers, but Hyland hasn’t been a one-game wonder. He scored in double figures in three of the last four contests. It’s perhaps not surprising that with more minutes, Hyland is scoring more and dishing out more assists. But the impressive thing is that he’s doing it without sacrificing any efficiency. Hyland’s Stats Show He’s Not Forcing Things Oct 31, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Bones Hyland (8) shoots over San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie (30) in the first half at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Hyland is a run-and-gun type combo guard who has the ball in his hands quite a bit when he’s on the floor, particularly now that Edwards isn’t playing. It would be easy for him to force shots and passes that aren’t there. But so far Hyland’s stats show that his increased production has come within the flow of the game and the Timberwolves’ offense. In fact, Hyland’s efficiency has increased along with his minutes. He was a dismal 2-10 (20%) from the field in his first four games but has shot 19-37 (51%) in the last four. Hyla

item.title: Packers special teams coach reveals Packers’ confidence level on Trey Smack
item.description: Green Bay Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack continues to receive support from special teams coordinator Cam Achord despite his recent struggles. Achord, who spent four seasons in the same role with the New England Patriots under Bill Belichick, expressed confidence in the young kicker on Tuesday and said he has no concerns about Smack’s confidence being shaken by his recent misses. Packers ST coach Cam Achord said he’s not worried about Trey Smack getting in his own head after repeated misses: “I think that’s why we picked him.” Also, Achord on Coleman Owen’s fumbled kickoff, he said they approach it like “you’ve got the fate of the team when the ball’s… pic.twitter.com/Pai9CmQBbB — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 3, 2026 The Packers ST coordinator made those comments after Smack recorded his eighth missed kick of the season in Green Bay’s 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, October 29. Achord also addressed another costly error from that game, when kick returner Coleman Owen lost a fumble on the opening kickoff. ESPN’s Rob Demovsky shared Achord’s remarks on Tuesday, noting that the coach does not believe Trey Smack is allowing his recent misses to affect his confidence or mindset. “I think that’s why we picked him,” he remarked. Trey Smack with the Green Bay Packers Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) attempts a field goal against Detroit Lions during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Achord’s comments indicate that Green Bay remains confident Smack can work through his early career struggles. The former Florida kicker has made 11-of-16 field-goal attempts across eight games, putting his conversion rate at 68.8%. He has also connected on 16 of 19 extra-point tries, leaving him with eight missed kicks overall this season. The Carolina game added another missed kick to Smack’s season, as his first-quarter extra-point attempt bounced off the left upright after Love found Kraft for a 12-yard touchdown. He made up for it by successfully converting all three of his remaining tries. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) watches a field goal miss during the first quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images His struggles had been more pronounced the previous week against Detroit. In the Packers’ 20-17 loss on October 25, the rookie failed to make a 26-yard field goal and saw his 35-yard attempt blocked. Those misses left him with only one successful conversion from three field-goal attempts. item.title: Every player from Arizona to play for the Boston Celtics - Jerryd Bayless
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from Arizona who have played for Boston. Our focus in this article is Jerryd Bayless. An alum of Arizona, he was picked up with the 2008 overall selection of the 2008 NBA Draft by the Indiana Pacers . The Phoenix, Arizona native played the first 2 seasons of his pro career with the Portland Trail Blazers instead. He also played for the (then) New Orleans Hornets (now, Pelicans), Toronto Raptors, and Memphis Grizzlies before he was dealt to the Celtics in 2014. His stay with the team lasted until he signed a deal with the Milwaukee Bucks that summer. During his time suiting up for the Celtics, Bayless put up 10.1 points, 2.1 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and 1.0 steals per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Kevin Durant shares what he thinks would be different about Shaquille O’Neal if he played in the NBA today
item.description: Photo by Don EMMERT / AFP via Getty Images Two-time NBA champion Kevin Durant believes that Shaquille O’Neal would continue to fill the stat sheet if he played in this era. Having won four championships in his career, Shaquille O’Neal retired as one of the most dominant players in the league. His strength and athleticism made it almost impossible to guard him, especially when he was playing alongside Kobe Bryant during his LA Lakers tenure. While discussing O’Neal’s game, the one thing that gets scrutinised is his inability to shoot the ball. However, Durant believes his dominance in the paint and passing as a big would allow the center to do so much even in today’s NBA. Kevin Durant feels Shaquille O’Neal would have way more space if he played in this era During the early 2000s, teams were not shooting much from the three-point line. In fact, during the 1999-2000 season, the average for three-pointers taken around the league was 13.7. This has now increased to 37.8 in the current season, which indicates how different the game is in the current era. However, Durant believes this would prove to be advantageous for the three-time Finals MVP, purely because of how dominant he was on the court. “I feel like it’s way more space for Shaq to operate, there’s way more skilled players, so he doesn’t have to do as much… Shaq would be getting triple-doubles, he would be getting more rebounds and he would score more points,” said Durant on The Rushmore podcast. Durant made this point about O’Neal while arguing that the current era of basketball is the best ever in the NBA. “There’s more shots going up, so more rebounds and there’s more shooters, so you could pass out of double teams. You could pass pretty well big fella, but he was passing to guys who couldn’t really shoot that well,” Durant added. The 54-year-old averaged 23.7 points and 10.9 rebounds for his career on 58.2% shooting from the field. While a big in today’s NBA is expected to shoot well, O’Neal made only 1 three-pointer throughout his career. If he played in today’s game, O’Neal would definitely have a lot of free throws, but even his shooting from the charity stripe was below average. However, his dominance in the paint alone would unlock the team’s offence. Alongside his offensive game, O’Neal was also brilliant on the defensive side of the game, averaging 2.3 blocks for his career. With him inside the paint, it would be difficult to imagine teams attacking the rim, as his presence alone would make things significantly harder. All these factors do make it clear that while O’Neal’s game is old-school, the way he played it would translate in any era of the league, which is why he will always be one of the best bigs the NBA has ever seen. item.title: Drone warfare in space: Swarms of autonomous, laser-shooting cubesats could defend Western satellites in orbit
item.description:
Mark is an award-winning freelance aviation and space journalist and author of the non-fiction book "N-4 DOWN: The Hunt for the Arctic airship Italia." He began writing for Space.com in 2026 and writes for a range of publications, from BBC Future to The Smithsonian’s Air and Space Quarterly and others. Mark won awards two years in a row at the Aerospace Media Awards for features he had written on the history of drones and astronaut training. Space grabbed hold of Mark’s imagination when, as a child, he saw the opening scene of "Star Wars: A New Hope" for the first time and has never let go. Away from the final frontier, Mark can be found walking his dog along the country lanes of England’s Cotswolds.

In May 2026, four Russian military satellites came close to ICEYE-X36, a private synthetic aperture radar satellite widely believed to be providing battlefield intelligence for Ukraine, in an apparently aggressive and risky "grey zone" maneuver that spooked many in the space industry. Close enough to jam or interfere with the satellite's signal, blind it with a laser, fire a metal dart at it or, simply, force it to maneuver and burn fuel, the satellites' seemingly intimidatory behavior has increased the West's desire to develop defensive technology for satellites . In October 2026, it was reported that one of those same four Russian satellites passed within 500 meters (1,650 feet) of the same ICEYE satellite. Now, U.K. startup Shield Space is racing to apply the lessons of drone warfare in Ukraine to develop swarms of up to 100 very small, low-cost, attritable drone-like autonomous spacecraft called cubesats . Released by a car-sized carrier in Earth orbit, these microwave-sized spacecraft will act as interceptors to protect Western satellites , and their deployment will mark a next step in the evolution of orbital warfare . Shield Space says that these space drones will use "effectors" like lasers or microwaves, or "kinetic standoff" techniques, to defend Western satellites even if controllers lose contact with them. "We're talking about deploying 100 cubesats on a protect-and-defend mission for less than £100 million [$134 million US], which is how [much] you would pay for one satellite previously," said Graeme Ritchie, co-founder and CEO of Shield Space. Launched in 2023, NASA's civilian project Starling demonstrated that a swarm of four small satellites can cooperate and operate autonomously in space on a civilian science mission without relying heavily on real-time commands from ground control. But that seems like a far cry from the adversarial or defensive missions Shield Space and its competitors imagine. It is telling that the leading space powers appear not to have demonstrated swarm combat in space — although they tend to be reluctant to reveal their space warfare capabilities. item.title: Taking stock of the Panthers cornerback room following the firing of Ejiro Evero
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches a touchdown pass against Will Lee III #24 of the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Panthers defeated the Eagles 25-14. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! We’re coming off a wild week following the most recent Panthers loss to the Packers, one that saw them decide to jettison defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. It was quite a jarring move to make in the middle of a season where despite a myriad of injuries along the defense, the Panthers still have a shot at the playoffs. As far as the Evero firing goes, I still haven’t quite settled on how I feel about it. I think I am currently leaning towards that it makes sense, but probably should have happened following the 2025 season rather than spending the 2026 off-season building around the scheme Evero would use. There were many questionable personnel decisions like not playing 2025 standout UDFA Corey Thornton or 3rd year CB Chau Smith-Wade, along with subbing out some of the younger guys with upside like Princely Umanmielen when the pass rush has struggled. All in all, I think the decision ultimately makes logical sense and I am looking forward to seeing what kind of changes the Panthers make post-Evero to try and right the ship, or at the very least keep it floating with duct tape until they get back Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, and Jaelan Phillips. The biggest question mark moving forward is going to be what the team does with their depleted CB room. Recently brought back coach and former cornerback DeAngelo Hall will have his work cut out for him. Let’s take a look at the current room as it stands. Will Lee III The 2026 4th round pick became the de facto CB1 following the injuries to Horn and Jackson. He’s logged 7 pass deflections in 7 games played and continues to progress after being thrown right into the fire. The Panthers planned on him being heavily involved early, as he manned one of the boundary spots in nickel formations when the cornerback room was fully healthy. Unfortunately, he is day to day right now with a hamstring injury, which means they may miss him for at least a game, possibly more depending on how his recovery goes. Not great, but the experience he’s getting this season as a 4th round rookie should prove very valuable from a long term perspective. Chau Smith-Wade The former 5th round pick played quite a bit since his rookie season in 2024. He’s played in 36 career games with 11 starts, though curiously his defensive snap counts went down this season following a career high 63% of snaps played on defense in 2025. This season, he’s only accounted for 21% of the defensive snaps, playing almost as many snaps on special teams (86) as he has on defense (88). item.title: Agent of veteran NFL coach shares whether Jerry Jones has contacted over Cowboys opportunity
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Jerry Jones has admitted he is not looking to move on from Brian Schottenheimer despite the Dallas Cowboys’ dreadful start to the season. The Cowboys suffered yet another defeat at AT&T Stadium on Sunday. This time, America’s team lost to the Arizona Cardinals and it was clear to see just how frustrated the result left Jones as the broadcast cameras captured his reaction. Dallas head into this weekend sitting in second spot of the NFC East but their 3-5 record leaves a lot to be desired. Playing the Indianapolis Colts this weekend will provide Schottenheimer with a massive opportunity to get a win under his belt. Despite what many analysts may be saying, Jones is not yet looking to replace Schottenheimer, and the agent of one veteran NFL coach has expressed the reason why that might be. What an agent of one veteran NFL coach has said about Jerry Jones One of the biggest issues Jones has suffered from over the years is not wanting to spend big on coaching staff. This has not been an issue for Jones when it comes to players, but he has often looked to find a bargain with his coaches. ESPN reporter Jane Slater shared the response she received from the agent of one veteran coach after she asked around about Jones potentially moving on from Schottenheimer. “I called the agent of a veteran coach to see if Jerry Jones had even picked up the phone and poked around on him during the Schottenheimer hiring cycle and he laughed and said “Jerry won’t pay 13M and up and that’s the starting point” It’s well known and well documented just surprised he actually finally said it on record today,” she said on X. It feels as if something has to change for the Cowboys to truly make a step in the right direction. The finances and belief have been shown by Jones in trying to improve the roster but it seems as if the coaching may still be holding the Cowboys back. However, Cowboys fans will also feel as if they have been saying this for decades, with their last Super Bowl trophy coming all the way back in 1996. If Schottenheimer cannot secure a win over the Colts, then it is hard to see how he could continue as the head coach. item.title: The LeBron James stat that shows why the Philadelphia 76ers are bound for the NBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers fans are already looking forward to a run to the 2027 NBA Finals after one specific LeBron James stat proves to be a major indicator. The 76ers are leading the Eastern Conference after the first two weeks of the 2026-27 NBA season, holding a 7-1 record with the team looking comfortable as the leading contenders in the East. The additions of LeBron and Jaylen Brown have been a major factor in enabling this success, with LeBron in particular bringing 23 years of experience with 10 Finals appearances and four championships. LeBron James’ career trend indicates the 76ers are NBA Finals-bound As mentioned, James has made the NBA Finals 10 times over his career. Every single time his team has started the season 7-1 (4 instances), they have invariably reached the Finals , with three NBA Championships being won in the process. LeBron led the 11-12 Heat, 15-16 Cavaliers, 16-17 Cavaliers, and 19-20 Lakers all to 7-1 starts in those respective seasons. Outside the 16-17 Cavaliers, each squad won the NBA title, with the 16-17 Cavaliers losing to the Golden State Warriors with Kevin Durant. If this career trend from James is to be held, the 76ers are bound to reach the NBA Finals in 2027. So far, they do look like the favourites to do so, with their closest rivals being the 6-1 Detroit Pistons, who still have roster flaws to work through. The 5-2 Boston Celtics are interesting opponents but might struggle to match up with the depth and talent of the 76ers, while other presumed contenders such as the 4-2 Toronto Raptors and 3-4 New York Knicks have had spotty starts to the season. If the trend of LeBron’s 7-1 teams going to the NBA Finals is to be broken, one of the East’s elites need to step up and stop the 76ers, who are looking like a well-organised machine far quicker than most anticipated. James is playing the perfect team-first role, averaging 16.2 points, 7.3 assists and 7.0 rebounds while playing some of the best defence we have seen from him in the last five years. item.title: Week 8, 3 down and 3 down: No silver lining from the Monsoon Bowl
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers rushes in the first half against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons played the role of Artax from The Neverending Story , and like Atreyu, Falcons fans’ cries and pleas went unanswered as they watched their team slowly drown in the swamp. There is no up this week; everyone sank in the pit. Here’s the Week 8, 3 down and 3 down. 3 down Michael Penix Jr. This is what the worst version of Penix looks like. The slow starts have been there all season, but the turnovers have not. He’s a rhythm passer, but that’s a two-way street; once he gets off beat, he stays there. When he finds his groove, he is one of the more efficient passers out there. Yes, the game plan was poor and so was the weather, but that doesn’t mean you carelessly throw off your back foot, or throw into double/triple coverage. Everyone has bad games; I don’t expect Penix to look this bad again, but it’s up to him to make sure that doesn’t happen. Michael Panix Bowles packed the line and once again Penix struggled with these looks. Rat defender ate his lunch all day, he struggled when forced to move and, mechanics deteriorated as things got worse and he compounded his bad decisions. Worst game of his career. pic.twitter.com/Rsx9i3eVlg — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 2, 2026 Matthew Bergeron The guard received his extension based on his potential, and he isn’t living up to it. Unlike others on the line, he isn’t a lineman with a typical outside-zone build; he has the physical traits that should transfer to a gap or duo scheme, but the team hasn’t had much success running these concepts behind him. Of all the Falcons linemen, he is the one who doesn’t get to use the size excuse many have applied to the Buccaneers -Falcons mismatch, but he was routinely manhandled. If Bergeron can’t turn things around, he’ll be the first black eye on Cunningham’s resume, because no matter how this season goes, they are tied to him through the 2027 season . Run Defense The Falcons didn’t allow a single reception in this game, but they did allow 324 rushing yards. The rookie linebackers struggled all game, and the attacking scheme’s aggressive nature is being taken advantage of by gap schemes, and Jeff Ulbrich is out of answers. He’s increased the number of defensive line slants, a technique that essentially has his defenders line up in one gap and shoot into another, but it doesn’t really solve the problem. For starters, it’s a guessing game; the defense doesn’t know where the ball is going and is hoping to catch the offense off guard, but they aren’t. The other issue is that against a gap scheme, they block down most of the time, so even if you move into a new gap, the OL isn’t necessarily unprepared; they just need to play sound and pick up whoever shows up. item.title: Lions scouting report: Dolphins’ strengths, weaknesses
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins throws a pass against the New England Patriots during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images After back-to-back stressful divisional victories at home, the Detroit Lions get a bit of a break and head down to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins. Detroit is on a three-game winning streak, and we’ve seen the defense take a step in the right direction to complement this offense. The Lions are finding their groove, it seems, and taking on a struggling team could be big for them. Miami is coming off another loss and aiming higher and higher at getting the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The team hasn’t been strong on either side of the ball; the offense is missing playmakers because of injuries or skill set, and while the defense has talent, it hasn’t had enough impact on the field. Let’s take a deep look at the Dolphins’ season so far as they head into Week 9. Miami Dolphins 2026 season thus far (1-6) Week 1: Lost to Las Vegas Raiders 27-13 Week 2: Lost to San Francisco 49ers 35-13 Week 3: Lost to Kansas City Chiefs 24-10 Week 4: Lost to Minnesota Vikings 15-10 Week 5: Lost to Cincinnati Bengals 31-24 Week 6: BYE Week 7: Defeated New York Jets 28-25 Week 8: Lost to New England Patriots 24-19 Offensive stats: The offense has been the roughest part of the Dolphins team this season. Newly signed quarterback Malik Willis was given the keys to the starting job, but the supporting cast isn’t the same as it was in Green Bay. He’s thrown for six touchdowns, five interceptions, and is averaging 181.1 yards per game. His legs have helped a lot, as he’s averaging 6.3 yards per carry, amassing 225 yards, and three touchdowns. When he isn’t running the ball, second-year running back Ollie Gordon is. Gordon took over for De’Von Achane after Achane tore his ACL in Week 3, ending his season. Gordon is averaging 4.5 yards per carry, with 408 yards and a team-high four rushing touchdowns, sparking an offense that desperately needs help. Willis has struggled to pass as well; his top wide receiver, Malik Washington, has 31 catches for 329 yards, and tight end Greg Dulcich has 22 catches for 256 yards. Receivers Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman have found the end zone most often among the group, combining for four touchdowns (two each) with 21 catches for 308 yards. Willis’ offensive line has also struggled to give him time to throw. According to PFF, the line has the second-lowest pass-blocking grade (53.6). Willis has been sacked 21 times this season, the seventh-highest in the NFL. Run blocking is better, but not by much, ranking 27th with a 55.9 grade. Miami has had to rely on the ground game to stay alive, as Willis just doesn’t have the time or the weapons in the passing attack to make teams nervous. item.title: Alphaball Twins League, season results: Alpha bats
item.description: A cycle by any other name smells as sweet. | Brace Hemmelgarn / Minnesota Twins / Getty Images …perhaps my wish for fewer absurd offensive seasons in these OOTP tournaments was wishful thinking. All-Star Break Let’s check in on those statistics and Yep, that’s the top six batters across the league hitting over .360 and who knows how many more with an OPS over 1.000. Why did I think this wouldn’t happen? And the players at the top of the board aren’t those I thought would be there; especially notable is top batter Jimmy Ryan, who played in the 1800s and is now dominating against players from all eras. At least the top pitchers are stars as always, and a lot of the expected names there: Johan Santana, Walter Johnson, Bobo Newsom, Lefty Gomez… Cole Irvin? Okay, there are some unexpected names too. And the standings: At least winning percentages are more balanced than previous tournaments, although Dezful, with nine wins more than any other team, is currently running away with the top seed, not just in the Omega League but across the board. The Alpha League’s top seed race is much closer as Sikasso and Warwick are separated by two wins (note that Sikasso has played two more games than Warwick). And the race for the bottom… every division’s got one. Also, since it’s the All-Star break: Norm Zauchin won the Home Run Derby Challenge, beating David Ortiz 17-11 in the final round, and the Omega League beat the Alpha League in the All-Star Game 2-1 on Chili Davis’s sixth-inning RBI single. End of Regular Season Were the Defenders able to hold onto their overall top seed? Yes they were! Dezful led the league with 103 wins and will be the top seed in the Omega half of the bracket, fending off a late charge from Alpha’s top seed Warwick. I didn’t set tiebreakers, so the game will decide that element between teams with the same record. The MacGuffins ended at the bottom of the league, probably due to having multiple pitchers who only appeared in one career game. Anything can happen in the playoffs, though! Statistically, though: We’ve got some shake-ups at the top of leaderboards: Taffy Wright passed Jimmy Ryan late to claim the batting crown, and Bob Johnson’s late-season surge made him the only player in the league to top 50 home runs. Ryan still dominated the batting stats, leading all hitters in WAR, runs, steals, OBP, slugging, and OPS (by deduction). On the pitching side, Walter Johnson continued to put up dominant performances, finishing with a sub-1.00 WHIP (199 hits, 51 walks, 253.1 innings) while also leading in WAR, strikeouts, innings, FIP, complete games, and K/BB. Surprisingly, Johan Santana dropped in some measures (4.1 WAR at the break, 5.0 WAR at season’s end), but he’s still very present among the leaderboards: fourth in strikeouts and third in a bucket of categories (ERA, innings, WHIP, K/BB, RA9/WAR, AVG against). item.title: In photos: How Ballhalla willed the Golden State Valkyries to a WNBA title
item.description: Golden State Valkyries players lift the WNBA championship trophy after winning Game 7 at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 31, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) From day one, the Golden State Valkyries' home court at Chase Center quickly garnered a reputation for its raucous and supportive crowds that sold out the arena night after night. Soon, people compared it to "Roaracle," the charged atmosphere inside Oakland Arena that hosted the Golden State Warriors before they moved across the bay to San Francisco. Valkyries fans came up with a fitting nickname as well: Ballhalla . "A lot of times in my head I'm like we got to do it for them," said Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes. "They're always here with us, like no matter we win, or we lose, we were getting that energy from them a lot." But although the analogy holds some truth, over the first two seasons of the team's existence, the Valkyries' home court has come to mean much more to many of their fans than just supporting a basketball team. Golden State Valkyries fans celebrate at the final whistle of Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 31, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) Fans wave rally flags during Game 7 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 31, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) Valkyries fans react to a score late in the fourth quarter during Game 1 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 17, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) It became a venue to support women and LGBTQ rights, often under attack these days in the United States. "I've said it multiple times that Ballhalla became my safe space," said Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams in an end-of-season exit interview where she noted that she received death threats for her support of transgender rights. More Valkyries - Valkyries MVP celebrates in the most low-key way imaginable - Details announced for Valkyries' WNBA championship parade - Amid tension of Game 7, Kaitlyn Chen wears hot dog costume - Protesters showed up at the WNBA Finals. Valkyries fans shut them down. Full Valkyries coverage For all of our Bay Area sports coverage, sign up for The Catch newsletter . One of the rallying cries for fans happened after the Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream on Pride Night on June 26. Williams found a camera on the court and yelled : "For the gays!" Many Valkyries fans, including a sizable queer presence, felt connected to the team that represented and brought joy to the San Francisco Bay Area. "This world is just a mess," Valkyries season ticket holder Cheryl Espinosa-Jones explained to SFGATE . "Joy is revolutionary." Valkyries fan Mcyb dances and holds a T-shirt during halftime of a viewing party at Thrive City outside Chase Center in San Francisco for Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream on Oct. 29, 2026.

item.title: Villanova has 20 reasons to feel better about its season-opening loss
item.description: Oh mio Dio! Villanova basketball’s trip to Rome for the Eternal City Tip-Off didn’t exactly end the way Wildcat fans had hoped. The Cats opened their 2026-27 season with a frustrating 74-72 loss to former Big East rival Notre Dame on Sunday, blowing a 10-point second-half lead in a game they probably should’ve won comfortably. But there’s a pretty good reason to feel optimistic about Kevin Willard’s squad after its first game. Actually, there are 20 of them. Nova turned the ball over 20 times against the Fighting Irish, including an almost-impressive 15 giveaways in the first half alone. The Irish turned those mistakes into 20 points, which is a pretty good way to lose a basketball game you otherwise controlled. And somehow, the turnovers weren’t the only problem. The Wildcats also surrendered 17 offensive rebounds, giving Notre Dame second and third chances on possessions that should’ve gone the other way. Between the turnovers and their inability to clean up the glass, Villanova essentially handed the Irish enough extra opportunities to steal a game they had little business winning. Here’s the encouraging part. Villanova shot 46.2% from the field compared to Notre Dame’s 35.4%. Willard’s squad made more shots despite attempting 13 fewer, held the lead for 83% of the game and looked like the better team for most of the afternoon. That’s pretty encouraging for a team still figuring out how to play together. Of course, nobody should be celebrating 20 turnovers or pretending the rebounding issues will magically fix themselves. Willard has plenty to clean up before Friday’s home opener against Holy Cross. But the Wildcats also cut their turnovers from 15 in the first half to five in the second, which suggests some of the sloppiness can be corrected as this group gets more comfortable playing together. It’s Game 1. There are going to be growing pains, especially with a roster that’s almost entirely new. Villanova already showed it can do everything else that’s required for a win. Taking better care of the basketball and finishing defensive possessions would go a long way toward turning those encouraging stretches of “what’s required to win” into actual wins. The loss stinks, especially considering it was against Notre Lame (ha(!), got em). But if Willard can clean up those two areas, there’s plenty to like about what the Wildcats showed in Italy.

item.title: Yankees’ 6-Year Slugger Miguel Andujar Cuts Ties With New Team After Unfortunate Injury
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - JUNE 15: Miguel Andujar #41 of the New York Yankees in action against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on June 15, 2018 in the Bronx borough of New York City. New York Yankees defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 5-0. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Yankees have plenty of questions to answer as they begin preparing for the next season. After another disappointing postseason exit, the franchise will need to evaluate its lineup and determine which additions could help it return to the World Series, all with the backdrop of a looming lockout set to disrupt the negotiating period between teams and players. And with several familiar players likely to depart in free agency, the Yankees will be searching for additional offensive depth this winter where they can find it. The team has now received an update involving a former six-year contributor whose latest season was interrupted by an unfortunate injury. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Phillies Infield Castoff Returns To Hated Division Rival After Cut Former New York Yankees Slugger Returns To Open Market After Unfortunate Season Miguel Andujar, who spent the first six seasons of his major league career in New York, is officially back on the open market after his first season with the San Diego Padres. “Miguel Andujar declined a 2027 mutual option,” the Padres announced last week . The decision was a bit of a formality, as the Padres were set to decline the option even if Andujar had opted in, but either way it means the 31-year-old will receive his buyout and become available to sign with any major league club. The Padres could still pursue a new agreement with him, but it seems his tenure in San Diego is at an end after an unfortunate wrist injury derailed his season. “Andujar signed a one-year deal with the Padres last winter worth $4MM in guaranteed money ($1.5MM in salary and $2.5MM via the buyout),” Mark Polishuk wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “Over 254 plate appearances, Andujar hit .259/.303/.423 with five homers, but he spent over two months on the injured list after a wayward Lucas Erceg pitch fractured his right wrist.” Andujar signed with San Diego last winter hoping to establish himself as a productive offensive contributor. He showed some promise before the injury and now could be seeking a longer-term deal with a new team. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees’ Former All-Star Gary Sanchez Declined By Brewers Shortly After World Series Win New York Yankees Once-Promising Slugger Seeks New Contract After Exit Andujar originally joined the Yankees in 2017 and emerged as one of their more promising young hitters the following season. In 2018, he finished second to Shohei Ohtani in American League Rookie of the Year voting after batting .297 with 27 home runs, 92 RBI and 47 doubles. item.title: Confirmed: Barcelona starlet Hamza Abdelkarim nominated for CAF Young Player of the Year award
item.description: Confirmed: Barcelona starlet Hamza Abdelkarim nominated for CAF Young Player of the Year award FC Barcelona starlet Hamza Abdelkarim has been nominated for the Confederations of African Football’s (CAF) Young Player of the Year award for 2026. The Egyptian striker finds himself in the final ten-man shortlist for the prestigious honour, along with other exciting African talents such as Manchester City’s Ayyoub Bouaddi. Recognition for Hamza’s growth The 18-year-old striker arrived at Barça in February earlier this year, signing on a loan deal from Al-Ahly on loan until the end of the season. The teenager excelled during the second half of the last season with the club’s Juvenil A (U19) side, making a big impression as he finished with six goals in nine league appearances. It prompted the Blaugrana to activate the permanent purchase clause in the loan agreement to acquire Abdelkarim’s services on a full-time basis during the summer transfer window. This came after he made his debut for the Egyptian national team and even represented them at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Since his permanent signing, Hamza has been drafted into the first-team dynamics under Hansi Flick and was a standout performer during the pre-season, scoring four goals. Minutes have been harder to come by once the season has started, but the teenage forward continues to be rated highly . Hamza Abdelkarim in the running for 2026 CAF Young Player of the Year prize. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Abdelkarim has played only 12 first-team minutes in 2026/27, while he has one goal from one appearance for Barça Atletic. Other nominees Owing to his progress with Barcelona and Egypt, Hamza has now earned a nomination for the CAF Young Player of the Year award for 2026. The 18-year-old prodigy will compete for the award alongside several highly regarded prospects, including Real Madrid’s Yan Diomande, Manchester City’s Bouaddi, Bayer Leverkusen duo Ibrahim Maza and Christian Kofane. The likes of Fiorentina’s Christ Inao, Coventry City’s Caleb Yirenkyi, Ismael Kamissoko of Academia Etoiles du Mandé, Ajax’s Abdellah Ouazane, and Aston Villa’s Ibrahim Mbaye have also been nominated.

item.title: 1 Fact, 1 Fiction: Michigan and Michigan State for the Paul Bunyan Trophy
item.description: A win is a win, and Michigan left Piscataway with one over Rutgers in the worst game for the Wolverines’ defense so far this season. After not allowing more than 20 points in a game through seven games, it was Rutgers of all teams that broke that streak. And while the offense showed some encouraging signs with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr, there are still plenty of questions heading into one of the most important games of the season against Michigan State — no matter what the Spartans’ record says. The Paul Bunyan Trophy is up for grabs this weekend, and Michigan — and its coaching staff, specifically — can’t afford to overlook its in-state rival. Fact: Jason Beck’s seat is still incredibly hot One Carr flu game isn’t going to be enough for Michigan fans to shy away from calling for offensive coordinator Jason Beck’s head. The Wolverines scored their most points in a conference game this season last week, but the offense still ranks 127th in total offense and second-last in the Big Ten in passing offense. Much of Michigan’s success came from the creativity of Carr to escape the pocket and take off. The run game still struggled as a collective, running for a little more than three yards per carry despite Savion Hiter logging 76 yards on 20 carries. The offensive line is still being shuffled around due to injury and can’t seem to find a rhythm. Beck still has much to figure out and not much time to do so. Michigan State also boasts one of the worst offenses in all of the FBS, but the Spartans’ defense is not nearly as bad as Rutgers. Michigan State is at 50th in yards allowed per game and 66th in points allowed per game. If the Spartans somehow find a way to win a low-scoring slugfest, it could be the end of the line for Beck. Fiction: Michigan State’s record and rivalry losing streak makes this like any other game The worst thing Kyle Whittingham and the coaching staff can do is treat Michigan State like any other game. Earlier in the week, Whittingham mentioned the intensity and “nastiness” of the rivalry, referencing the tunnel incident from 2022. He also said the in-state rivalry is “not the biggest one, but it’s a big one.” All those are exactly the trap Whittingham could fall into that leads the Spartans to win. Although Michigan has won the last four meetings in the rivalry — as well as Michigan State losing six straight games this season and remaining winless in conference play — there’s still everything to lose for the Wolverines. It’s hard to feel convinced Whittingham understands the pure physicality that takes place in the rivalry, given what he’s said about it. Michigan State might not be having the season it envisioned, but this game is circled on the calendar for the Spartans despite also having a first-year head coach in Pat Fitzgerald. Michigan has the more talented roster, the better record and the recent history on its side, but none of that matters if the Wolverines come out flat and allow Michigan State to dictate the physic

item.title: Why fast start means more for Texas now, SEC coach concerns and Longhorns' youth takeover | Bohls
item.description: Rasheem Biles (3) and Texas could use another fast start against Missouri given the Longhorns' issues during the second half of recent games. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - While I got ya, here are nine things and one crazy prediction: 1. On your mark, get set… It's imperative that the Texas football team gets off to a fast start. Naturally every team wants to come out of the gates strong, especially on the road, and Texas has done that lately. The Longhorns jumped out to a 17-3 lead on Florida late in the first half, a 24-3 edge on Ole Miss at halftime and a 17-0 lead on Mississippi State . Two of them worked out well. If they fall behind Missouri on Saturday , the Tigers will just pound away with their powerful running back tandem and wear Texas down. Of course, teams playing on the road always want to score early and often to silence the sellout crowd, but it's even more critical for this Texas team since it has scored only 10 points in the third quarter in five SEC games and is more banged up now than at any other point in the season. It could be without its All-American left tackle, All-American edge rusher, two receivers, two defensive backs and its best wide receiver. Yikes. That would be a lot to overcome. If Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo can't go, Texas would be without its two premier receivers or, what Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz called "game-wreckers. They can wreck the scoreboard with a single play." … "I think we're a tough, hard-nosed football team," head coach Steve Sarkisian said Monday. "We're not always the prettiest team right now, but we sure know how to be at our best when our best is needed. Now we've got to be better. We've got a lot of grit." … I would think the 11 a.m. kickoff is more favorable for Texas because the fans might not be as riled up. A fast start presumably would entail better rushing from a Longhorn team that produced 60 yards rushing against Mississippi State and 61 yards at Tennessee and 99 yards versus Florida and been fortunate enough to win two of those. But Texas' ground game has, well, run aground. I can't remember the last time its rushing attack has looked this weak unless it was maybe last season when no running back topped even 600 yards. The Longhorns ran for a paltry number against the Bulldogs with their reconfigured offensive line and a brand new starter at right tackle in Andre Cojoe. Sarkisian knows it and has to do something drastic to move the chains and keep his own defense off the field. … On the flip side, Will Muschamp's defense must keep Missouri's run game in check. Asked how Texas did last week, linebacker Rasheem Biles said, "I'd give us a B." But a B won't cut it against the Tigers. Ahmad Hardy, arguably the best rusher in college football a year ago, is back and figures more prominently in Missouri's rotation with Jamal Roberts, Drinkwitz said this week. item.title: NBA Power Rankings for all 30 teams after opening weeks of new season
item.description: (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images So much can change in the NBA in just a couple weeks, and it’s already happened to start the 2026-27 season. A massive rash of injuries has decimated the playing field, leaving some teams trying to tread water until their stars return, and others needing to find new solutions with key pieces out for the foreseeable future. No team has been hit harder than the Oklahoma City Thunder , who are missing Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace with long-term injuries that threaten their status as a contender. Some teams already look dead in the water to start the season, and it’s not just perennial doormats like the Sacramento Kings and Chicago Bulls. The Phoenix Suns and Utah Jazz hoped to break into the playoff picture this year, but they’ve both been just awful to begin this year. Meanwhile, there are a few teams potentially making the jump from good to great who deserve to be taken seriously the rest of the way. There are some major changes from our last set of power rankings when training camp opened . Let’s rank every team in the league so far. 30. Sacramento Kings : One of the wildest stats of the young season is Darius Acuff being tied with Luka Doncic for the league lead in field goal attempts per game so far. Acuff needs to scale back his shot volume and start to get some of his veteran teammates more involved to reach his ceiling, but ultimately nothing is saving this Kings team this year. 29. Los Angeles Clippers : The Clippers just don’t have anything they can hang their hat on to start the year. Darius Garland is turning the ball over constantly, Keaton Wagler can’t score from two-point range, and there’s just not enough size in the front court. This team is bad, bad. 28. Milwaukee Bucks : It was always going to be a long year for the Bucks after the Giannis trade, and it’s already proving true. This team is dreadful on both ends despite head coach Taylor Jenkins doing a good job of helping them stay in games to start the year. Tyler Herro has been cooking so far, and his eventual trade deadline deal might be the one thing to look forward to the rest of this season beyond their rookies’ development. 27. Chicago Bulls : The good news is that Caleb Wilson has been outstanding, and might already be the team’s best player. The bad news is that Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey are struggling to fit in around the rookie forward, which might put this Bulls’ rebuild back to square one around their new franchise player. Chicago’s perimeter defense is atrocious, it’s not a good rebounding team, and it’s dead-last in three-point percentage. It’s going to be a long year, but Wilson’s activity on both ends is a thrilling sign for the future. 26. Brooklyn Nets : The Nets had five first round draft picks in 2025, and it was immediately obvious that they blew it in the moment . Three of them are fully out of the rotation to start their second season, and even Egor Demin, the best pick of the bunch

item.title: 2026 WNBA season review: Was this just the beginning of the Golden State Valkyries dynasty?
item.description: The Golden State Valkyries. | Getty Images The Golden State Valkyries have defied the odds at every turn. In their first season, they broke records by selling out every home game and posting a WNBA-high attendance total. The Valkyries also reached the playoffs in that opening year, the first expansion team to do so. Somehow, their second season was even grander. Golden State dominated the league, posting the best defense in the regular season and earning the No. 2 seed. They took that momentum and proved they had no rival in 2026, beating the Atlanta Dream in seven games in the WNBA Finals to win their first title. The sound of a season coming full circle. You came for this. Now come celebrate it. See you on the Embarcadero tomorrow, Ballhalla. pic.twitter.com/j8wGKoFv1T — Golden State Valkyries (@valkyries) November 3, 2026 Accomplishing this so quickly is absurd . And while this might be shocking for many fans, it is not for their owner, Joe Lacob. He set the timeline for the Valkyries to win it all at five years. They did it in less than half that time. Here what Lacob declared when the Valkyries were introduced just over three years ago: First press conference with the Warriors, I said we will win a championship in the first five years. And I’m telling you right now, we will win a WNBA championship in the first five years of this franchise. Put this in your bookmarks. @wnbagoldenstate owner Joseph Lacob vows that once play begins, they will win a championship in the first 5 years of their existence 🙌 pic.twitter.com/Xxa5limkMz — WNBA (@WNBA) October 5, 2023 So, let’s take a look at what went right for Golden State, allowing them to achieve Lacob’s ambitious dream, as well as what, if anything, went wrong and what might be next. What went right for Golden State ? There are plenty of great stories surrounding the Valkyries, but none better than Gabby Williams . Playing for three teams in eight years, Williams hadn’t found a place where she could permanently hone her skills. If she desires, Golden State can be her forever home. Gabby Williams is named the 2026 WNBA Finals MVP 🏆 She averaged 19.6 PPG, 3.6 RPG, 2.6 SPG & 2.7 APG Williams was a consistent force in the Finals to help the @valkyries earn their first-ever Championship! #WNBASeason30 | #2026WNBAFinals pic.twitter.com/0STG6e1pE4 — WNBA (@WNBA) November 1, 2026 Williams had a career year for the Valkyries. She averaged 14.4 points and shot 34.2 percent from 3-point range. Add in her defensive versatility and 1.6 steals per game, and it’s no wonder she was an All-Star, made the All-Defense Team and even garnered some MVP votes. When the Valkyries needed her most, she delivered. In Game 7, Williams scored 30 points, securing the win and winning Finals MVP. What went wrong for Golden State ? When you win, who cares what went wrong? The goal is to win it all, and when you do, you can take any criticism; the counterargument is the ring. Still, basketball never stops, and next year will be her

item.title: Arizona football notebook: Moving forward, embracing expectations and investing in the community
item.description: TUCSON, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Brent Brennan of the Arizona Wildcats interacts with fans before the game against the Iowa State Cyclones at Casino Del Sol Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Tucson, Arizona. (Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona has to quickly move forward from its heartbreaking 34-26 loss to Texas Tech and focus on the Friday night matchup against TCU. However, while preparation needs to turn to the Horned Frogs, lessons learned from the trip to Lubbock cannot be ignored. For fifth year linebacker Chase Kennedy , he is entering the endgame of his time as a Wildcat, which means that those lessons need to be learned and applied quickly. That’s what makes it perfect timing for the short week due to a Friday night tilt with TCU. “Each game, each week, this week especially just because of the quick turnaround, that you would necessarily want to forget about because there’s a lot of lessons to be learned from that game,” said Kennedy. “You got to be able to move on just because each week is a new opponent, and that’s it.” Even the great ones miss The leader of the Wildcats, Noah Fifita , also needs to be one of those players who quickly forgets what happened against Texas Tech. He was unable to seize a possible “Heisman moment” but there is still a lot of football to be played. Offensive coordinator Seth Doege gave a lot of credit to his quarterback and said he was the main reason Arizona had a chance to beat Texas Tech. “The truth is, and what I told him afterwards, we’re only in that game because of Noah Fifita,” said Doege. “That’s the only reason we’re in that game. So if anybody has any other opinion about that, you’ve lost your mind, because they literally said we’re not going to let number one beat us and he almost did. Playing like drop eight tampa two coverage. There’s nowhere to throw the football, and he found ways to throw for 417 yards.” After Fifita missed his throw to Tyler Powell on a critical fourth down against Texas Tech, Fifita immediately apologized to Doege once he got on the headset. Doege did not need an apology because “Number One” was the reason Arizona was in a position to win the game. “Even the greatest ones miss,” said Doege. “It was unfortunate, and I know it eats at him.” While Fifita and the Wildcats missed out on a big opportunity, the month of November can still present more opportunities to accomplish goals set out in August. That includes Fifita being a Heisman candidate as he moved up two spots in the fan vote standings to number seven. item.title: Tottenham and Chelsea battling Arsenal for Serie A star
item.description: Tottenham and Chelsea battling Arsenal for Serie A star Gustavo Varela joined Monza from Benfica B this season and has quickly established himself as one of the standout performers in Serie A. His impressive displays have reportedly attracted interest from Arsenal , who are monitoring his progress. The striker has been outstanding in the Italian top flight, and his performances suggest that Monza could struggle to keep him if interest from bigger clubs continues to grow. Several top sides are reportedly considering a move for the youngster . Arsenal have a strong interest in recruiting talented young players, particularly those who demonstrate exceptional ability at an early stage of their careers. Varela has certainly attracted attention with his performances since the beginning of the campaign. Arsenal face competition for Varela The striker has scored nine goals in as many Serie A appearances, an impressive return that has made him one of the most exciting prospects in Italian football this season. Arsenal are reportedly interested in signing him, but Fussball News reports they face competition from Tottenham and Chelsea, with both London clubs also following his progress closely. Although the campaign is still at an early stage, Varela appears capable of reaching double figures in the near future. His goalscoring record is particularly impressive considering he is playing for a smaller club rather than one of Italy’s established giants. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Summer move could be more realistic A January transfer to the Emirates Stadium may prove difficult to complete, particularly if Monza are reluctant to lose such an important player midway through the season. However, a summer move could become a realistic possibility if Varela maintains his current form and continues scoring regularly. Arsenal will undoubtedly face competition if his performances attract further attention, but his age, goalscoring ability and impressive start to life in Italy make him an interesting prospect. The Gunners could consider making their move at the end of the campaign. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Morning Report | Coach questions if UFC influenced controversial referee standup: ‘If you don’t fight a certain fight, you’re not getting in’
item.description: Tom Nolan and Renato Moicano at UFC Vegas 123﻿ | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC In the aftermath of UFC Vegas 123, headliners Tom Nolan and Renato Moicano have been overshadowed by a controversial call and what it said about the current state of the UFC. Referee Dan Miragliotta has been widely criticized for calling for a standup with Moicano attacking Nolan from back control, which led to Nolan rocking Moicano with a knee in the closing moments of the second round before finding a finish in the third. It was the sixth straight win for Nolan, who also collected a $100,000 Performance of the Night bonus. Veteran coach Ray Longo discussed the situation on the Anik & Florian Podcast, questioning whether there are greater forces at work when a referee takes that kind of action. “I want to know if Dan, there was anything from the top that led him to do that,” Longo said. “I don’t think he’s deciding to do that on his own, that’s how bad it was. I just can’t see it. And we know that the UFC, when you hold a guy against the cage, they don’t even let you on the Contender Series. I tell my guys this, you’re saying effective coaching, for the guys that go on the Contender, you know what they’re looking for. If you don’t do it, I don’t want to hear any complaining. “Now, is that right? I don’t want to coach like that. It’s not right for me. I want to be an MMA coach and come up with a strategy to get a win, but you can’t do that anymore. If you don’t fight a certain fight, you’re not getting in that organization.” Longo also wondered if there were more subtle ways of manipulating how Nolan and the ending of the fight are perceived. Cageside analyst Daniel Cormier criticized Miragliotta’s decision live, while also trying to shine the spotlight on Nolan, which Longo sees as a half-measure. “Let me just say one other thing, I think the thing is we’ve got to say it every f*cking week at the start of the show,” Longo said. “You just don’t let it go. ‘DC,’ he did do a good job, everyone’s in a weird spot. They have jobs, their families are dependent on a paycheck. He did try, but to say, ‘I don’t want to make it about Moicano, make it more about Tom.’ No, f*ck that, what are you talking about? The guy got gifted something. What do you mean make it about Tom Nolan? “I’m not attacking DC, I’m just saying he tried. I think if you want to make change, you’ve got to stay on it, that’s all I’m saying. You can’t let it go next week, everybody’s talking about something else.” The UFC Vegas 123 main event left such a bitter taste in Longo’s mouth, he couldn’t even fully appreciate Nolan’s efforts. Nolan later defended the result, suggesting “that’s how it would have gone” even without Miragliotta’s intervention. Longo wishes Nolan had acknowledged the officiating assist. “It just kind of ruined the fight for me,” Longo said. “I’ve never, ever seen anything like that in my life. It was interesting to update the TD:INT ratio chart this week as Jared Goff fell out of the top ten and Dak Prescott replaced him while Joe Burrow fell below Patrick Mahomes after his wild performance on Sunday. Caleb added a to his ratio with the one TD while Rodgers threw a pick (yay!) and closed the gap ever so slightly. The Bucs defense is playing good football and will be another good challenge for this offense. After the bye, the Bears square up against the Saints, Lions, Jags, and Dolphins in what could be a stretch to really stack some big point totals. We’re not quite halfway through the season and Rome Odunze and Luther Burden have looked the part of an incredible one-two punch. Statistically, giving a slight correction weighting Caleb’s appearances, they both look like they’ve got a good chance at going over the 1,000 yard mark.
